newsitem.title: FRANCE: G7 backs peaceful solution to Peru hostage crisis.
newsitem.headline: G7 backs peaceful solution to Peru hostage crisis.

text.p: The Group of Seven (G7) industrialised nations and Russia said on Friday they supported Peru's efforts to end the 10-day hostage crisis at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima peacefully.
A G7 communique issued by France, which holds the group's rotating presidency, said the G7 "reaffirmed the general principle under which no concession must be made in the face of a terrorist action".
G7 countries "express their solidarity with the Peruvian government and support its efforts to resolve the crisis peacefully, with the main objective of sparing human lives", the statement said.
"They are prepared, individually and collectively, to help the Peruvian government by using all the appropriate means that it could request," it said.
The group said no political or ideological aim could justify the attack on the Japanese embassy in Lima where Marxist guerrillas are holding more than 100 hostages.
Japan revealed earlier in the day that it was consulting fellow G7 members to try to work out a solution to the crisis.
